In [[probability theory]] and [[statistics]], the '''hyperbolic secant distribution''' is a continuous [[probability distribution]] whose [[probability density function]] and [[Characteristic function (probability theory)|characteristic function]] are proportional to the [[hyperbolic function|hyperbolic secant function]]. The hyperbolic secant function is equivalent to the reciprocal [[Hyperbolic function|hyperbolic cosine]], and thus this distribution is also called the '''inverse-cosh distribution'''.

Generalisation of the distribution gives rise to the '''Meixner distribution''', also known as the '''Natural Exponential Family - Generalised Hyperbolic Secant''' or '''NEF-GHS distribution'''.

== Definitions ==

=== Probability density function ===

A [[random variable]] follows a hyperbolic secant distribution if its probability density function can be related to the following standard form of density function by a location and shift transformation:

:<math>f(x) = \frac12 \operatorname{sech}\frac{\pi x}{2},</math>

where "sech" denotes the hyperbolic secant function.

=== Cumulative distribution function ===

The [[cumulative distribution function]] (cdf) of the standard distribution is a scaled and shifted version of the [[Gudermannian function]],

:<math>\begin{align}
F(x) &= \frac12 + {\frac{1}{\pi} \arctan} \Bigl({\operatorname{sinh}\frac{\pi x}2}\Bigr) \\[8mu]
&= {\frac{2}{\pi} \arctan}\Bigl({\exp\frac{\pi x}2} \Bigr) .
\end{align}</math>

where "arctan" is the [[trigonometric function#Inverse functions|inverse (circular) tangent function]].

Johnson et al. (1995)<ref>{{cite book |first1=Norman L. |last1=Johnson |first2=Samuel |last2=Kotz |first3=N. |last3=Balakrishnan |year=1995 |title=Continuous Univariate Distributions |volume=2 |isbn=978-0-471-58494-0}}</ref>{{rp|page=147}} places this distribution in the context of a class of generalized forms of the [[logistic distribution]], but use a different parameterisation of the standard distribution compared to that here. Ding (2014)<ref>{{cite journal |last=Ding |first=P. |year=2014 |title=Three occurrences of the hyperbolic-secant distribution |journal=The American Statistician |volume=68 |pages=32–35 |citeseerx=10.1.1.755.3298 |doi=10.1080/00031305.2013.867902|s2cid=88513895 }}</ref> shows three occurrences of the Hyperbolic secant distribution in statistical modeling and inference.

== Properties ==

The hyperbolic secant distribution shares many properties with the standard [[normal distribution]]: it is symmetric with unit [[variance]] and zero [[expected value|mean]], [[median]] and [[mode (statistics)|mode]], and its probability density function is proportional to its characteristic function. However, the hyperbolic secant distribution is [[kurtosis#Terminology and examples|''leptokurtic'']]; that is, it has a more acute peak near its mean, and heavier tails, compared with the standard normal distribution. Both the hyperbolic secant distribution and the [[logistic distribution]] are special cases of the [[Champernowne distribution]], which has exponential tails.

The inverse cdf (or quantile function) for a uniform variate 0 ≤ p < 1 is

:<math>F^{-1}(p) = -\frac{2}{\pi}\, \operatorname{arsinh}\!\left[\cot(\pi\,p)\right] \! ,</math>
:<math> = \frac{2}{\pi}\, \ln\!\left[\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\,p\right)\right] \! .</math>

where "arsinh" is the [[inverse hyperbolic function|inverse hyperbolic sine function]] and "cot" is the [[trigonometric function|(circular) cotangent function]].

== Generalisations ==
=== Convolution ===
Considering the (scaled) sum of <math>r</math> [[independent identically distributed random variables|independent and identically distributed]] hyperbolic secant random variables:
:<math>X = \frac{1}{\sqrt{r}}\; (X_1 + X_2 + \;...\; + X_r)</math>
then in the limit <math>r\to\infty</math> the distribution of <math>X</math> will tend to the normal distribution <math>N(0,1)</math>, in accordance with the [[central limit theorem]].

This allows a convenient family of distributions to be defined with properties intermediate between the hyperbolic secant and the normal distribution, controlled by the shape parameter <math>r</math>, which can be extended to non-integer values via the [[Characteristic function (probability theory)|characteristic function]]
:<math>\varphi(t) = \big(\operatorname{sech}(t /\sqrt{r})\big)^r</math>

Moments can be readily calculated from the characteristic function.  The excess [[kurtosis]] is found to be <math>2/r</math>.

=== Location and scale ===

The distribution (and its generalisations) can also trivially be shifted and scaled in the usual way to give a corresponding [[location-scale family]]:

:<math>f(x) = \frac{1}{2 \sigma} \operatorname{sech} \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}\right)</math>

=== Skew ===

A [[skewness|skewed]] form of the distribution can be obtained by multiplying by the exponential <math>e^{\theta x}, |{\theta}|<{\pi}/2 </math> and normalising, to give the distribution
:<math>f(x) = \cos \theta \; \frac{e^{\theta x}}{2 \operatorname{cosh}(\frac{\pi x}{2})} </math>
where the parameter value <math>\theta = 0</math> corresponds to the original distribution.

=== Kurtosis ===

The [[Champernowne distribution]] has an additional parameter to shape the core or wings.

=== Meixner distribution ===

Allowing all four of the adjustments above gives distribution with four parameters, controlling shape, skew, location, and scale respectively, called either the '''Meixner distribution'''<ref>[https://reference.wolfram.com/language/ref/MeixnerDistribution.html MeixnerDistribution], [[Wolfram Language]] documentation. Accessed 9 June 2020</ref> after [[Josef Meixner]] who first investigated the family, or the '''NEF-GHS distribution''' ([[Natural exponential family]] - Generalised Hyperbolic Secant distribution).

In [[financial mathematics]] the Meixner distribution has been used to model non-Gaussian movement of stock-prices, with applications including the pricing of [[Option (finance)|options]].

=== Related distribution ===

Losev (1989) has studied independently the asymmetric (skewed) curve {{nowrap|<math>h(x)=\frac{1}{\exp(-a x) + \exp(b x)}</math>,}} which uses just two parameters <math>a, b</math>. In it, <math>a</math> is a measure of left skew and <math>b</math> a measure of right skew, in case the parameters are both positive. They have to be both positive or negative, with <math>a = b</math> being the hyperbolic secant - and therefore symmetric - and <math>h(x)^r</math> being its further reshaped form.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Losev |first=A. |title=A new lineshape for fitting X‐ray photoelectron peaks |journal=Surface and Interface Analysis |volume=14 |issue=12 |year=1989 |pages=845–849 |doi=10.1002/sia.740141207}}</ref>

The normalising constant is as follows:
:<math>\frac{a+b}{\pi}\sin\left(\frac{b \pi}{a+b}\right)</math>

which reduces to <math>\frac{2a}{\pi}</math> for the symmetric version.

Furthermore, for the symmetric version, <math>a</math> can be estimated as <math>a=\frac{\pi}{2\sigma}</math>.
